text: ALLERGY IS A SAFETY ALERT, NOT A PREFERENCE. Verify against the authorised source and food-safety process; never rely on a face match alone.

preview: CANDIDATE | POSSIBLE SAME-STAY ACTION | VALIDATION QUESTION

text: The oat-milk example is synthetic and does not describe a verified PARKROYAL workflow or guest preference. Ask the partner which guest-approved detail staff can act on in the lounge and share across roles. Preferences and allergies have different operational meanings. Allergy details require verification against the authoritative hotel source and food-safety process; a face match alone cannot support an allergy decision. W3C use-of-color guidance: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html .

The steps describe a proposed service journey. The main hotel POC and standalone Rokid demo are separate systems. The main POC simulates taps, an active lounge cohort, synthetic records, matching and a cue path. The standalone demo uses a local gallery and displays a name/status; it does not capture a preference or integrate with the hotel profile. New preference capture and cross-staff sharing are proposed, not demonstrated.

name: slide-11-status-copy
text: CURRENT MAIN HOTEL POC: simulated tap/cohort, synthetic profiles, matching and cue path.  |  SEPARATE ROKID DEMO: local gallery match + name/status; not integrated.  |  RV101 frame delivery and hotel data access remain validation gates.

This slide adds a proposed guest-approved write path to the separate lounge retrieval architecture. Staff enters and reviews a short note, confirms the guest and current stay, and saves a stay-scoped record with source/time/expiry metadata. The mock-hotel API and SQLite are synthetic POC components. lounge-control handles tap events, active cohort and profile lookup; face-worker matches against the current candidate set; Android is the RV101 vendor bridge. The main hotel POC simulates core flow components. The standalone Rokid demo is separate and does not use this profile path. RV101 continuous/sufficiently frequent frames, hotel data access, role permissions, retention, recognition reliability and cue readability need validation.
